title: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
venue: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for a comprehensive benchmark to evaluate large language models (LLMs) in Chinese, particularly on advanced knowledge and reasoning tasks. The authors argue that most prominent benchmarks are English-centric and do not adequately capture knowledge domains relevant to Chinese users, such as Chinese history, law, politics, and school curricula. To address this gap, they introduce C-EVAL, a Chinese evaluation suite intended to measure foundation models' performance across a wide range of subjects and difficulty levels.

The approach is the construction and validation of a benchmark rather than an educational intervention study. C-EVAL contains 13,948 multiple-choice questions spanning 52 disciplines across four levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional exams. The authors also introduce C-EVAL HARD, a subset focused on especially difficult reasoning-heavy subjects such as advanced mathematics, chemistry, and physics. They evaluate 11 existing LLMs, including GPT-4, ChatGPT, Claude, GLM-130B, and others, under zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting settings.

There are no human learner participants in the study. The context is benchmark development and model evaluation using exam-style questions drawn from mock exams, local exams, university exams, and other publicly available Chinese assessment materials. Although the benchmark includes middle- and high-school subject matter, the paper does not study K-12 students, teachers, or classrooms.

The main conclusion is that current LLMs still have substantial room for improvement on advanced Chinese knowledge and reasoning tasks. GPT-4 is the only evaluated model to exceed 60% average accuracy on C-EVAL, and even it performs only modestly on the harder subset. The authors conclude that C-EVAL can serve as a useful diagnostic tool for analyzing strengths and weaknesses of foundation models in Chinese, especially beyond casual conversation and into more demanding reasoning contexts.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a benchmark and model-evaluation dataset paper, not a K-12 educational intervention study. It evaluates foundation models on exam-style Chinese multiple-choice items and does not report any learner-facing implementation, instructional comparator, or student outcome methodology.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no direct evidence of impact on K-12 students, teachers, literacy instruction, or educational outcomes. Reported results are model benchmark accuracies only, so no educational intervention effect can be inferred.
